chunks: And do not disgrace me on the day when they are raised
ai.seo_question: What does the Quranic verse 'And do not disgrace me on the day when they are raised' mean?
ai.summary: This verse, situated within Surah Ash-Shu'ara, serves as a pivotal supplication by the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him and his progeny) to seek protection from the disgrace of being rejected by God on the Day of Judgment. In Shia exegesis, it underscores the concept of 'Izzah' (honor) derived solely from divine favor, contrasting with worldly status, and highlights the believer's reliance on God's mercy amidst the accountability of the Hereafter. The phrase 'Yawma Yub'athun' (the Day they are raised) emphasizes the universal resurrection, a core tenet in both Sunni and Shia eschatology, where all souls will stand before the Creator.
